debutant.question: What event marks the beginning of the Bible?
debutant.explanation: The Bible begins with the story of God's creation of the world in 6 days (Genesis 1).

debutant.question: In what chronological order did these events occur?
debutant.explanation: The order is: Abraham (c. 2000 BC) → Moses (c. 1300 BC) → David (c. 1000 BC) → Jesus (c. 1 BC).

debutant.question: How many days did it take God to create the world?
debutant.explanation: God created in 6 days and rested on the 7th day (Genesis 1-2).

debutant.question: How many years did the Israelites wander in the desert?
debutant.explanation: The Israelites wandered for 40 years in the wilderness because of their lack of faith (Numbers 14:33).

debutant.question: What was the first event following the creation of man?
options: The fall of Adam and Eve
debutant.explanation: After the creation of Adam and Eve, the Bible recounts their sin and fall in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 3).

debutant.question: Before or after the flood was the Tower of Babel located?
options: The Tower of Babel and the Flood are simultaneous
debutant.explanation: The Tower of Babel was built after the flood by Noah's descendants (Genesis 11:1-9).

debutant.question: Which king reigned before David in Israel?
debutant.explanation: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel before David succeeded him (1 Samuel 9-11).

debutant.question: Who reigned after David?
debutant.explanation: Solomon, son of David, succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 1-2).

debutant.question: What event followed the death of Solomon?
options: The division of the kingdom in two
debutant.explanation: After Solomon's death, the kingdom was divided into two: Israel in the north and Judah in the south (1 Kings 12).

debutant.question: Which people destroyed Jerusalem and took the Jews into exile?
debutant.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple in 586 BC. (2 Kings 25).

debutant.question: Who allowed the Jews to return to Israel after the Babylonian exile?
debutant.explanation: Cyrus the Great of Persia issued an edict in 538 BC. allowing Jews to return to Israel (Ezra 1:1-4).

debutant.question: In what period of history was the birth of Jesus located?
options: Under the reign of Herod the Great and the Roman Empire
During the reign of Alexander the Great
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born during the reign of Herod the Great, when Judea was under Roman rule (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: What event marks the beginning of the Christian Church?
debutant.explanation: Pentecost, 50 days after Easter, marks the birth of the Church with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2).

debutant.question: In what order did these events of the Passion occur?
debutant.explanation: Order: The Last Supper (Thursday evening) → Gethsemane and arrest → trial → Crucifixion (Friday) → Resurrection (Sunday morning).

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus appear after his resurrection before his ascension?
debutant.explanation: Jesus manifested himself for 40 days after his resurrection before ascending to heaven (Acts 1:3).

intermediaire.question: In what chronological order should these patriarchs be placed: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob?
intermediaire.explanation: Order: Noah (after creation) → Abraham (c. 2000 BC) → Isaac (his son) → Jacob (son of Isaac).

intermediaire.question: When was the first Temple in Jerusalem destroyed?
intermediaire.explanation: Solomon's Temple was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar in 586 BC. BC during the capture of Jerusalem.

intermediaire.question: What period approximately corresponds to Moses historically?
intermediaire.explanation: Most historians place Moses and the Exodus around 1280-1250 BC. BC under Ramses II of Egypt.

intermediaire.question: In what order do the great empires of Daniel 2 follow one another?
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel 2 and 7: Babylon (gold) → Persia (silver) → Greece (brass) → Rome (iron). Order corresponding to historical succession.

intermediaire.question: When did the prophets Amos and Hosea prophesie?
options: Period of the United Kingdom under David/Solomon
Period of the divided kingdom (8th century BC)
intermediaire.explanation: Amos and Hosea prophesied in the 8th century BC (around 760-720), in the Northern Kingdom, shortly before the fall of Samaria (722 BC).

intermediaire.question: What is the approximate date of the writing of the oldest Gospel?
intermediaire.explanation: Mark, considered the oldest gospel, is generally dated to 65-70 AD. BC, before or after the destruction of the Temple.

intermediaire.question: When did the city of Samaria (Northern Kingdom) fall?
intermediaire.explanation: Samaria fell in 722 BC. BC under Sargon II of Assyria, leading to the deportation of the 10 tribes (2 Kings 17).

intermediaire.question: When did Paul write his epistles chronologically?
intermediaire.explanation: The Epistles of Paul (c. 50-62 AD) are the oldest NT texts, predating the written Gospels.

intermediaire.question: In what chronological order should these books of the NT be placed: John, Mark, Acts, Revelation?
intermediaire.explanation: Approximate dating: Mark (65-70) → Acts (80-85) → John (90-95) → Revelation (95-96 AD).

intermediaire.question: When did Alexander the Great conquer Judea?
intermediaire.explanation: Alexander the Great conquered Palestine in 333-332 BC. BC, opening the Hellenistic period which would have a profound impact on Judaism.

intermediaire.question: Approximately how long did Abraham and Jesus last?
intermediaire.explanation: Abraham is dated around 2000 BC. BC and Jesus was born around 4-6 BC. BC, approximately 2000 years apart.

intermediaire.question: Approximately when did the destruction of the Second Temple take place?
intermediaire.explanation: The Second Temple was destroyed by Titus and the Roman armies in 70 AD. BC, as Jesus prophesied (Matthew 24:2).

intermediaire.question: What OT event immediately precedes the period of Judges?
options: The conquest of Canaan under Joshua
intermediaire.explanation: The conquest of Canaan under Joshua immediately precedes the period of the Judges. After Joshua's death, each tribe had its own rulers (Judges 1-2).

intermediaire.question: When did Jeremiah prophesy about the Babylonian exile?
options: Before and during the exile (from approximately 627 BC until 586)
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah began prophesying in 627 BC. (reign of Josiah) and continued through the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: In what order did the 3 kings of the United Kingdom reign?
intermediaire.explanation: Order of the first 3 kings: Saul (around 1050-1010) → David (around 1010-970) → Solomon (around 970-931 BC).

expert.question: What is the generally accepted date for the division of the Kingdom of Israel?
expert.explanation: The division of the kingdom under Rehoboam is conventionally dated to 931 BC. BC, after the death of Solomon.

expert.question: What is the main challenge of the 'Judges timeline' in biblical studies?
options: The sum of the years of the Judges totals over 400 years while 1 Kings 6:1 speaks of 480 years between the Exodus and the Temple
expert.explanation: Classic problem: the cumulative sum of the periods of the Judges exceeds 400 years. The solution: some periods overlap and are regional, not national.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the number '40' in biblical chronology (40 years of desert, 40 days of flood, etc.)?
options: A symbolic Hebrew number denoting a period of complete testing/transformation, without excluding historical reality
A purely ritual number without history
expert.explanation: The Hebrew '40' is both potentially literal AND loaded with symbolic meaning (full proof). We must not oppose symbolism and history.

expert.question: What is the high vs. low dating of the Exodus and what are the implications?
options: High dating: ~1446 BC. (1 Kings 6:1); low: ~1270 BC (Ramses II). The issue: the identity of the Pharaoh of the Exodus and the archaeological correspondence
The Exodus is universally dated to 1300 BC. AD
The debate is purely theological without historical basis
expert.explanation: 1 Kings 6:1: 480 years before the Temple (970 BC) = ~1446 BC (Thoutmosis III?). The low dating (~1270) follows Ramses II and the city of Pi-Ramses.

expert.question: What is the chronological framework of documentary theory (JEDP) concerning the writing of the Pentateuch?
options: Entirely in the time of Moses (around 1300 BC)
Sources J (900 BC), E (800), D (622), P (500-400) — Pentateuch finalized around 400 BC AD
Written in the 2nd century BC. AD
expert.explanation: Documentary theory classifies: Yahwist (J, ~900), Elohist (E, ~800), Deuteronomist (D, ~622), Priestly (P, ~500-450). Strongly contested by evangelicals.

expert.question: When and how was the NT canon officially established?
options: Progressively from the 2nd to the 4th century, with the canon of Athanasius (367 AD) and the councils of Carthage (397, 419)
By a formal apostolic decision of the 1st century
expert.explanation: The process of canonization of the NT: increasing use since the 2nd century, list of Athanasius (367), Council of Carthage (397) confirming the 27 books.

expert.question: How did the writing of the Gospel of John date in relation to the Johannine epistles and the Apocalypse?
options: Gospel (~90-95) → Epistles (95-100) → Apocalypse (95-96 or earlier under Nero)
Apocalypse written before the Gospel according to Neronian dating
Both dates are also attested in the manuscripts
expert.explanation: Dominant dating: Gospel of John (~90-95), Epistles John (~90-100), Apocalypse (~95-96 under Domitian, or ~65-68 under Nero according to Neronian dating).

expert.question: What is the chronological relationship between the epistles of Paul and the writing of the synoptic gospels?
options: The epistles of Paul (50-62) precede the synoptic gospels (Mark ~65-70; Matthew and Luke ~80-85)
expert.explanation: The Pauline epistles (50-62 AD) constitute the oldest written Christian texts we have, predating the written gospels.

expert.question: What is the challenge of OT 'absolute chronology' versus internal biblical chronology?
options: No challenge: the two match perfectly
The sum of the years of the kings of Israel and Judah does not correspond exactly to the Assyrian and Babylonian chronologies, requiring corrections for coregencies
expert.explanation: Thiele's royal lists (1951): numerous coregencies and different counting systems explain the apparent discrepancies. Synchronization with Assyria and Babylon is possible within ±1-2 years.

expert.question: What is the theological significance of the concept of 'fullness of times' (Galatians 4:4) in biblical chronology?
options: The conviction that the incarnation arrives at the precise moment desired by God: pax romana, Greek koiné, Jewish diaspora, intensified messianic expectation
A purely eschatological concept of the future
expert.explanation: The 'pleroma tou chronou' (Galatians 4:4): the Pax Romana (safe roads), the common Greek language, the global Jewish diaspora and intensified messianic expectation created a unique providential context.

expert.question: What is the difference between the 'chronos' and 'kairos' calendar in biblical theology of time?
options: 'Chronos' = sequential quantitative time; 'Kairos' = opportune moment charged with theological and decisive meaning — God's time in history
expert.explanation: 'Chronos' (χρόνος) = succession of measurable time. 'Kairos' (καιρός) = decisive, timely and theologically charged moment. The Incarnation is the Kairos par excellence (Mark 1:15).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'millennium' in Revelation 20 and the 3 major interpretations?
options: A literal future reign of 1000 years: only interpretation
(1) Premillennialism: future literal reign; (2) Amillennialism: symbolic period (Church era); (3) Postmillennialism: gradual reign before the return of Christ
expert.explanation: The 3 positions: (1) Premillennialism — Christ returns BEFORE the literal millennium; (2) Amillennialism — the millennium = present reign of Christ (patristic majority); (3) Postmillennialism — the millennium precedes the return of Christ.

expert.question: What is the dating of the book of Daniel and the debate between prophetic interpretation and Maccabean writing?
options: Lives. (internal date of the author Daniel) vs. 2nd c. (165 BC, critical position: 'prophecies after the fact' of the Maccabean era)
expert.explanation: Daniel appears as written in the 6th century. (Babylonian exile). Historical criticism dates its writing to ~165 BC. (Antiochus IV) — 'vaticinium ex eventu'. Issue: the possibility of predictive prophecy.

expert.question: What is the chronological relationship between the Jewish Passover and the death of Jesus according to the synopsis of the gospels?
options: The synoptics place the Last Supper on the evening of Passover; John places it on the day before (14 Nisan) — classic tension in exegesis
John and the synoptics are identical
The date is impossible to determine
expert.explanation: Classic tension: synoptics (the Last Supper = paschal meal, 15 Nisan) vs John (Jesus dies on 14 Nisan, when the paschal lamb was being immolated). Several solutions proposed.

expert.question: What is the chronological framework of the Protestant Reformation and its relationship with the rediscovery of the Bible?
expert.explanation: The Protestant Reformation: Luther published his 95 theses in 1517. The invention of printing (Gutenberg ~1450) and the rediscovery of NT Greek (Erasmus 1516) made possible the diffusion of the Bible in vernacular languages.
